facts.statement: The type specimen of Hauffiopteryx is an articulated complete skeleton (GPIT 1491/4) that preserved the skull and some soft tissues.
facts.quote: Hauffiopteryx is known from the lectotype GPIT 1491/4, articulated complete skeleton which preserved the skull and some soft tissues.

facts.statement: The lectotype specimen of Hauffiopteryx measures approximately 1.93 meters in length.
facts.quote: The animal is about 1.93 m in length.

facts.statement: Hauffiopteryx fossils from Germany and Luxembourg date to the early Toarcian stage of the Early Jurassic, between approximately 182.7 and 181.8 million years ago.
facts.quote: They were collected from the Harpoceras semicelatum-elegantulum-exaratum ammonoid subzones (Lias ε II1-5, about 182.7-181.8 mya), Harpoceras tenuicostatum-falcifer zones, of the Posidonia Shale.

facts.statement: Additional juvenile and infant specimens of Hauffiopteryx were discovered in the early Toarcian of Ilminster, Somerset, United Kingdom.
facts.quote: Additional materials were described by Hannah Caine and Michael J. Benton in 2011, from the early Toarcian of Strawberry Bank, Ilminster of England.

facts.statement: Hauffiopteryx is a relatively small ichthyosaur that reached lengths between 2 and 3 meters.
facts.quote: Hauffiopteryx is a relatively small ichthyosaur, reaching 2 - 3 m in length.

facts.statement: Hauffiopteryx possessed a short, very thin snout that tapered to a point.
facts.quote: The snout of Hauffiopteryx is short, but also very thin, tapering to a point.

facts.statement: The tooth crowns of Hauffiopteryx had smooth outer surfaces, with the rear teeth being larger than the front ones.
facts.quote: The outer surface of the tooth crowns is smooth, and the back teeth are larger than those in front.

facts.statement: The eye sockets of Hauffiopteryx typicus were notably large and circular.
facts.quote: The orbits (eye sockets) of H. typicus are especially large and circular.

facts.statement: The dorsal ribs of Hauffiopteryx were strongly forked at their upper ends, giving them a double-headed appearance.
facts.quote: The upper ends of the dorsal ribs (those in the trunk region) are strongly forked, making them double-headed.

facts.statement: Hauffiopteryx had four main digits in each forelimb, with some elements on the front edge featuring indentations.
facts.quote: Each forelimb contains four main digits, and the front edge of the limb consists of some elements with indentations on their front edges.

facts.statement: Unlike the four digits in the forelimbs, each hindlimb of Hauffiopteryx possessed only three main digits.
facts.quote: While the front edges of the hindlimbs contain some notched elements like the forelimbs, there are only three main digits in each rear limb.

facts.statement: The genus name Hauffiopteryx honors the Hauff family of Holzmaden for their work on the Posidonia Shale and combines the Greek word for 'fin' or 'wing'.
facts.quote: The generic name honors the Hauff family from Holzmaden, for their generation-long work to increase the knowledge on the Posidonia Shale and its fauna, especially the ichthyosaurs, and pteryx (πτερυξ), Greek for "fin" or "wing".

facts.statement: In Hauffiopteryx altera, the highest points of the upper jaw are located behind the nostrils, whereas in H. typicus they are located beneath them.
facts.quote: In H. altera, the tallest points of the maxillae (rear upper tooth-bearing bones) are positioned behind the external nares (openings that housed the nostrils), in contrast to H. typicus, where the tallest points are instead located beneath these openings.

facts.statement: The lacrimal bones differ between species: they are triradiate in H. typicus but massive and triangular in H. altera.
facts.quote: A further difference between the two species lies in the shape of their lacrimals; in H. typicus, they are triradiate, while those of H. altera are massive and triangular.

facts.statement: In Hauffiopteryx, the fibula (rear shin bone) is significantly larger than the tibia (front shin bone).
facts.quote: The fibulae are also much larger than the tibiae (front shin bones).

facts.statement: Michael W. Maisch originally described Hauffiopteryx based on specimens previously referred to Stenopterygius hauffianus.
facts.quote: Hauffiopteryx fue descrito originalmente por Michael W. Maisch sobre la base de algunos especímenes que fueron previamente referidos a Stenopterygius hauffianus.

facts.statement: The species is known from lectotype GPIT 1491/4, a complete articulated skeleton preserving the skull and some soft tissues.
facts.quote: Hauffiopteryx es conocido a partir del lectotipo GPIT 1491/4, un esqueleto completo y articulado que preserva el cráneo y algunos tejidos blandos.

facts.statement: The animal measured approximately 1.93 meters in length.
facts.quote: El animal mide cerca de 1.93 metros de largo.

facts.statement: It lived during the early Toarcian of the Early Jurassic, approximately 182 million years ago, in the Posidonia Shale of Holzmaden.
facts.quote: Fue recuperado de las subzonas de los ammonites Harpoceras elegantulum-exaratum (más específicamente Lias ε II4), y la zona de Harpoceras falcifer, del conocido lagerstätte Esquisto de Posidonia (Posidonien-Schiefer) de Holzmaden, datando de principios del Toarciano del Jurásico Inferior, hace cerca de 182 millones de años.

facts.statement: Specimens have been found in Holzmaden, Germany, and Dudelange, Luxembourg.
facts.quote: Especímenes referidos de Holzmaden, Alemania y Dudelange en Luxemburgo incluyen MHH '9', WAT 1, SMNS 51552, SMNS 80225 y probablemente el pobremente preservado SMNS 81965.

facts.statement: Additional materials were described by Hannah Caine and Michael J. Benton in 2011 from the early Toarcian of Strawberry Bank, Ilminster, England.
facts.quote: Materiales adicionales fueron descritos por Hannah Caine y Michael J. Benton en 2011, de principios del Toarciano de Strawberry Bank, Ilminster en Inglaterra.

facts.statement: The English specimens described by Caine and Benton are all juveniles or infants that preserved nearly the entire skeleton and some skulls.
facts.quote: Los ejemplares son todos juveniles o infantes los cuales preservaron casi todo el esqueleto y algunos cráneos.

facts.statement: Researchers found that Hauffiopteryx could be either a basal member of Eurhinosauria or a basal member of Thunnosauria, equivalent to the most basal member of Stenopterygiidae excluding Ichthyosaurus.
facts.quote: Tanto la descripción original de Maisch como la redescripción de los ejemplares ingleses encontraron que Hauffiopteryx podía ser tanto un miembro basal de Eurhinosauria o un miembro basal de Thunnosauria (lo cual es una posición equivalente a ser el miembro más basal de Stenopterygiidae sensu Maisch [2008] con la exclusión de Ichthyosaurus).

facts.statement: Friedrich von Huene originally recognized Hauffiopteryx in 1931 as a subspecies of S. hauffianus named Stenopterygius hauffianus typica.
facts.quote: Hauffiopteryx fue originalmente reconocido por Friedrich von Huene en 1931 como una subespecie de S. hauffianus siendo nombrado Stenopterygius hauffianus typica.

facts.statement: Michael W. Maisch elevated it to species rank and reassigned it to its own genus, Hauffiopteryx, in 2008.
facts.quote: Michael W. Maisch en 2008 lo elevó al rango de especie y lo reasignó a su propio género, Hauffiopteryx.

facts.statement: The genus name honors the Hauff family of Holzmaden for their work on the Posidonia Shale fauna, especially ichthyosaurs, and combines it with the Greek word for fin or wing.
facts.quote: El nombre del género honra a la familia Hauff de Holzmaden, por su trabajo a lo largo de una generación para incrementar el conocimiento del Esquisto de Posidonia y su fauna, especialmente los ictiosaurios, y pteryx (πτερυξ), término griego para "aleta" o "ala".

facts.statement: The parent group of Hauffiopteryx is Neoichthyosauria.
facts.quote: Parent group: Neoichthyosauria

facts.statement: Hauffiopteryx is classified in the class Reptilia.
facts.quote: Class: Reptilia

facts.statement: The time range for Hauffiopteryx is the Toarcian, from 184.2 to 182.9 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Toarcian to Toarcian (184.2 to 182.9 million years ago)

rejected.statement: The genus Hauffiopteryx was first described by Michael W. Maisch in 2008 based on specimens previously assigned to Stenopterygius hauffianus.
rejected.quote: Hauffiopteryx was first described by Michael W. Maisch on the basis of some specimens that previously referred to Stenopterygius hauffianus.

rejected.statement: Researchers suggest that Hauffiopteryx might be either a basalmost member of Eurhinosauria or a basalmost member of Thunnosauria.
rejected.quote: Both the original description by Maisch and the redescription of the English specimens found that Hauffiopteryx might be either a basalmost member of Eurhinosauria or a basalmost member of Thunnosauria.
